oneLiner: The No. 2 custom AI chip designer and the leading supplier of optical DSPs that link AI clusters, now trying to buy the laser maker Lumentum with stock. The market is betting that the deal dilutes holders and that AI capex peaks before the custom ramp management has promised for FY2028-FY2029 shows up.

verdict.stance: Positive - deal overhang, size for volatility
verdict.summary: Since October the operating story got better and the equity story got worse: management raised FY2028 revenue to ~$20B, then agreed to issue roughly half its share count again for Lumentum, and the AI complex derated around it. On standalone FY2028 non-GAAP EPS the scenarios skew up: the base case needs a little less than the company's own framework at a mid-20s multiple, while the bear case needs both a missed ramp and a peak-cycle multiple. We stay positive but small, because the deal parks the stock until it closes in 2028 and GAAP earnings are about a third of the non-GAAP figure we value. The view changes if the Dec 1 guide implies FY2028 below ~$18B, or if deal disclosures show EPS dilution with no synergy bridge.
wtb: FY2028 (year ending Jan 2028) revenue reaches at least ~$19B against management's ~$20B; the first test is a Q4 FY2027 guide near $3.7B on Dec 1, 2026.
Non-GAAP gross margin holds at 57.5% or better and non-GAAP operating margin reaches ~40% in FY2028, giving a ~34-35% non-GAAP net margin.
The market still pays ~24x standalone FY2028 non-GAAP EPS in January 2028, which requires the more-than-$12B FY2029 custom target to remain credible and 2027 hyperscaler capex guides to rise.
Diluted shares stay below ~940M before the Lumentum close, and the deal's pro forma EPS dilution is no worse than ~5% before synergies.

bear.why: 2027 hyperscaler capex flattens (state-level data center pauses, digestion), the custom ramp slips a generation and a contested socket is lost; revenue grows ~33% instead of ~67% and non-GAAP net margin stalls near 30% as opex was built for $20B. The market treats FY2028 as a peak, doubts the FY2029 custom target and prices in Lumentum dilution, paying a peak-cycle 15x.

base.why: Custom and 1.6T optics ramp roughly on schedule but supply and one program slip keep the year ~5% under the ~$20B framework; gross margin ~58%, operating margin ~40%, net margin ~34.5%. FY2029 growth of 35-40% is visible, which would justify ~30x, but the pending all-stock deal and a derated sector hold the multiple at 24x (about 17x FY2029 earnings).

bull.why: The framework is beaten: scale-up optics and the key-hyperscaler programs pull forward, operating margin reaches ~41% and net margin ~36%. 2027 capex guides rise again, regulators clear Lumentum with a credible accretion bridge, and FY2029 custom above $12B looks underwritten, so the market pays a growth multiple of 30x.

scenarioModel.note: EPS is NON-GAAP diluted (excludes stock comp, amortization and deal costs; Q2 FY27 GAAP EPS was $0.33 vs non-GAAP $0.94), standalone, before any Lumentum shares. EPS = revenue x non-GAAP net margin / ~935M diluted shares (Q3 FY27 guide ~921M plus warrant vesting and stock comp net of buybacks): bear $16B x 30% = $4.8B; base $19B x 34.5% = $6.56B; bull $21B x 36% = $7.56B. Net margin = operating margin less ~$145M other expense and a ~13% tax rate. Multiples apply to FY2028 EPS at end-January 2028. Inputs are Siberforge estimates, not consensus; no FY2028 EPS consensus could be verified (vendor forward EPS ~$7.4, period unverified).

debates.q: Does the Lumentum deal add or subtract value per share?
debates.bull: Lasers are the scarcest part of the optical link; owning them plus DSPs, drivers and Celestial's photonics gives Marvell the full stack as scale-up moves from copper to optics. Management claims more than $1B of run-rate cost synergies and non-GAAP EPS accretion in year one.
debates.bear: Lumentum holders get ~33% of the company. Press reports of Bank of America's model (unverified) show EPS 4.9% lower in calendar 2028 and 14.7% lower in 2030 without revenue synergies; the fixed ratio was struck near the highs; and optical module makers that buy Marvell DSPs become competitors.
debates.view: Do not pay for synergies. We value the standalone business and take roughly two multiple turns off the base case for the overhang; the deal is neither a reason to buy nor, at a fixed ratio with both stocks down, a reason to sell.

signpost.metric: Pro forma EPS bridge and synergy phasing on the Q3 call and in the S-4; regulatory filings
signpost.threshold: bullish if accretion is shown before revenue synergies; bearish if no bridge is given or a China review pushes the timetable past the Nov 1, 2027 outside date
signpost.when: Dec 1, 2026 call; S-4 expected early 2027 (timing unverified)

debates.bull: The framework has been raised at every update in 2026 and FY2027's ~$12B implies a Q4 near $3.7B, already a ~$15B run-rate. 18 custom sockets are won (5 XPU, 13 XPU-attach) and the key-hyperscaler agreement carries ~$120B of cumulative revenue potential over about six years.
debates.bear: Custom is still under $4B in FY2028 by management's own arithmetic, so the year leans on optics supply that needed $1B of prepayments. Benchmark's Dec 2025 claim that Trainium 3 and 4 went to Alchip was never confirmed or denied (unverified).
debates.view: Believe ~$19B, not $20B: the base case carries a 5% haircut for supply and one program slip. A guide that keeps FY2027 at ~$12B confirms it; anything softer moves weight to the bear case.

signpost.metric: Q4 FY2027 revenue guide and Q3 data center growth
signpost.threshold: on track if the guide is $3.6B or more and data center grew ~75% YoY; bearish below $3.4B or if the ~$20B framework is not repeated

debates.q: Does AI capex keep rising in 2027, or was October the peak multiple?
debates.bull: Nvidia raised its FY2028 growth outlook to ~75% on Nov 17 with supply as the limit, and custom chips plus optics are the fastest-growing lines inside that spend.
debates.bear: The sector derated on politics and governance, not numbers: new governors in Texas, Ohio and Georgia campaigned on pausing data center construction (per Motley Fool), and Nvidia's CEO resigned on Nov 12. Marvell's FY2031 target of $70-90B needs five more boom years that nobody has contracted.
debates.view: Capex decides the multiple (15x vs 30x), not FY2028 revenue, which is largely booked. The scenarios give the peak case a 30% weight; hyperscaler guides in early 2027 are the test.

signpost.metric: Combined 2027 capex guidance from MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META
signpost.threshold: bullish if guided up 25%+ YoY; bearish if flat or if a large state enacts a data center moratorium
signpost.when: Q4 calls, late Jan to early Feb 2027

debates.q: How much of the non-GAAP profit belongs to shareholders?
debates.bull: Cash backs the non-GAAP view: trailing free cash flow was $1.9B on $10.3B of revenue (12 months to Aug 1, 2026), and the excluded amortization is a non-cash relic of past deals.
debates.bear: Stock comp is a real cost: Q2 FY27 GAAP operating expenses were $385M above non-GAAP, against $200M of buybacks. Diluted shares rose 5.8% YoY (Celestial added ~27M), trailing GAAP net income was only 43% of operating income, and the hyperscaler warrant can add up to ~59M shares.
debates.view: Accept non-GAAP EPS for valuation but charge for it: the scenarios assume the share count keeps creeping up to ~935M and use multiples below what the growth alone would earn. A buyback pause during the merger would make this worse.

signpost.metric: Diluted share count and GAAP EPS as a share of non-GAAP EPS
signpost.threshold: red flag if diluted shares exceed ~925M or GAAP EPS falls below 45% of non-GAAP (the Q3 guide implies ~48%)

thesis: Guidance has only gone up. At the Oct 6 Investor Day FY2028 revenue was lifted from ~$18B to ~$20B (+67%), with data center at ~$18B (+80%), and the Nov 2 pre-announcement kept the Q3 midpoint.

Custom silicon has a multi-year backlog. Custom revenue was ~$1.5B in FY2026 and is targeted above $12B in FY2029 (more than triple FY2028) and ~$30B in FY2031, about 13% of a $235B calendar-2030 market by Marvell's sizing.

Interconnect is the scarce layer. Data center interconnect is expected to pass $1B in FY2028 from ~$500M in FY2026, scale-out switching also passes $1B, and scale-up optics (Celestial's Photonic Fabric) starts at a few hundred million dollars next year.

Operating leverage is arriving. Non-GAAP operating margin was 36.6% in Q2 FY27 (+180bp YoY) and is guided into the 38-40% target range in Q4 FY27, with FY2028 operating expenses growing at about half the rate of revenue.
The price fell while the numbers rose. The shares lost more than half their value between Oct 7 and Nov 5 on the deal and a sector selloff, with no cut to any revenue framework.
risks: The Lumentum deal is a very large dilution. Each Lumentum share converts into 4.5 Marvell shares (roughly 450M new shares by our arithmetic on a ~921M base), closing is not expected until the first half of calendar 2028, and Marvell owes a $3.2B fee if regulators block it.

Reported profit is a fraction of adjusted profit. The scenarios use non-GAAP EPS; GAAP operating margin was 16.8% in Q2 FY27 against 36.6% non-GAAP, and the difference (stock comp, amortization, deal costs) is why cash flow runs at 3-4x GAAP net income.

A handful of customers decide the outcome. Data center was 79% of Q2 FY27 revenue and custom programs are re-bid each generation; management says more than 35 sockets at the top four US hyperscalers deliver the vast majority of its long-term target.
Growth arrives at lower margins. Non-GAAP gross margin is guided to 57.5-58.5% through FY2028, below Q2's 58.9%, as custom scales; the FY2031 model allows 56-59%.

The valuation needs a long boom. The page's reverse DCF asks for mid-20s percent annual free cash flow growth for a decade, against ~14% a year revenue growth over the last three fiscal years, which included an inventory downturn.

latestProse: No new quarter since the last revision: Q3 FY2027 is scheduled for Dec 1, 2026 after the close (call 1:30pm PT). The last full print, Q2 FY2027, was a small beat on revenue with data center at 79% of sales, and operating cash flow dipped q/q because Marvell is prepaying suppliers (~$1B planned in FY2027) for 1.6T optical DSP and 51.2T switch capacity. What changed since is strategic. On Oct 6 the Investor Day raised FY2028 and introduced a FY2031 range of $70-90B with non-GAAP EPS above $30. On Nov 2 Marvell agreed to acquire Lumentum in an all-stock deal with an implied enterprise value of $115B, a 23.9% premium to the Oct 28 unaffected prices, leaving Marvell holders with ~67% of the combined company; the companies cite a $550B combined addressable market.
guidanceProse: Q3 FY2027 guide (Aug 27, narrowed Nov 2): revenue $3.15B plus or minus 2% (+15% QoQ, ~+52% YoY), non-GAAP EPS $1.10 plus or minus $0.05, GAAP EPS $0.48-$0.58, ~921M diluted shares, data center up more than 20% QoQ. FY2027 revenue ~$12B (+~45%), which with $8.31B in the first three quarters at guide leaves ~$3.7B for Q4. FY2028: ~$20B, non-GAAP tax rate ~13%. Deal terms that matter for guidance: the merger agreement's outside date is Nov 1, 2027, extendable in steps to Aug 1, 2028 for regulatory approvals; both shareholder bases must vote; termination fees are $5.8B (Marvell) and $2.9B (Lumentum) for a change of recommendation or superior proposal. Marvell has not said whether buybacks continue while the deal is pending (unverified).
segments: Data center (~79% of revenue): custom XPU and XPU-attach chips, optical DSPs and drivers, scale-out Ethernet switching (Teralynx), storage. Guided to grow ~60% in FY2027 and ~80% in FY2028.
Communications and other (~21%): carrier, enterprise networking, automotive and industrial; modelled by management at only ~$2.5B in FY2031.
Lumentum (pending, not in any number here): lasers and optical components; its Dec-quarter revenue guide is $1.575-1.625B.
competitive: Broadcom: the dominant custom-ASIC and switching rival and the incumbent at Google's TPU; Marvell's FY2031 custom target implies only ~13% share.
Alchip, MediaTek, GUC: lower-cost design-service challengers that contest each new hyperscaler generation.
Nvidia: merchant GPUs still take most cluster spend and its co-packaged optics push sets the pace for scale-up links.
Credo, Astera Labs, Broadcom, MaxLinear: connectivity and DSP rivals; Marvell leads in PAM4 optical DSPs.
Optical module makers (customers for DSPs today) would compete with a combined Marvell-Lumentum, as would Coherent in lasers.
moat: Multi-generation co-design relationships with hyperscalers, leading PAM4 DSP and SerDes IP, and a portfolio that spans electrical and optical links. Switching costs are high inside a program but low between generations, so the moat is per socket and has to be re-won; prepaid supply and, if it closes, in-house lasers add a capacity edge.
catalysts: Dec 1, 2026: Q3 FY2027 results and Q4 guide; first Q&A on the Lumentum accretion bridge (debates 1, 2, 4).
Mid-Dec 2026: Broadcom Q4 FY2026 report - AI semiconductor guide as the custom-ASIC read (debate 2).
Late Jan to early Feb 2027: hyperscaler Q4 calls with 2027 capex guidance (debate 3).
Early Mar 2027: Q4 FY2027 results and the first formal FY2028 quarterly guide (debate 2).
During 2027: S-4, shareholder votes and antitrust reviews; outside date Nov 1, 2027, close expected first half of 2028 (debate 1).

valPresets.note: FCF basis works because operating cash flow is strong, but supply prepayments and Celestial earnouts are real cash claims, stock comp is a cost the DCF ignores, and the pending Lumentum share issuance is not in the share count.
